sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: online with a Harvard login (also: harvard online access (harvardkey))
sources.note: Nothing. Covers 19 consonants + 6 vowels, diphthongs, vowel sequences, gemination, clusters, syllable types (mono- to pentasyllabic words); no suprasegmental section, no mention of stress, accent or tone anywhere (full text grepped and summary pp. 82-83 read).

sources.citation: Perumalsamy, P. 2011. Toto. In: Linguistic Survey of India: West Bengal, Part I, pp. 628-702. Kolkata/New Delhi: Language Division, Office of the Registrar General, India.
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: not located online or at Harvard
sources.note: Silent on stress/accent. The only prosodic-type features treated are 'Length' and 'Nasalization' (printed p. 652, PDF p. 672), both judged non-phonemic. Conclusion (printed p. 693, PDF p. 713): 'a. The tonal and pronominalizing features are not found in the Toto language'.
Segment inventory after Basumatary 2014; nothing on tone or stress.

sources.citation: Anderson, Deborah (Script Encoding Initiative, UC Berkeley). 2019. Proposal for encoding the Toto script in the SMP of the UCS. Unicode Technical Committee document L2/19-330, 27 Sept 2019, 12 pp. (phonological notes credited to fieldworker Toby Anderson; based on Anderson & Abhishek Toto 2018, Toto Writer's Guide, unpublished).
sources.note: Nothing on stress. States Toto has contrastive tone, p. 1: 'Tone is only used when the lack of it would confuse two words (the same could be said of vowel length). When tone is used it can either be rising or falling, and it is pronounced across the entire word (or phrase) - most easily heard in the final syllable. Tone is carried in the lexical stem but generally heard most in the suffix morphemes.' Also contrastive vowel length and breathy front vowels (Figures 9-10 give four-way tone x length sets, e.g. /nowa/ 'thinking' falling vs rising 'coming out'). Contradicts Perumalsamy 2011 on tone.

sources.citation: Anderson, Deborah (SEI). 2019. Introducing the Toto script. Unicode document L2/19-278.
sources.note: Earlier draft of L2/19-330; same tone/length/breathiness paragraph; nothing on stress.
